panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Post-contrast T1 MRI in a 4-year-old with cPACNS demonstrates middle cerebral artery wall enhancement, a classic imaging sign of vascular inflammation in primary angiitis of the CNS. B: DWI MRI shows restricted diffusion in the left basal ganglia representing an acute ischemic infarct secondary to childhood primary angiitis of the CNS. C: TOF MRA demonstrates stenosis of the middle cerebral artery, consistent with vasculitic large-vessel narrowing in childhood primary angiitis of the CNS.

in_text_mentions: A right frontal brain biopsy showed numerous perivascular non-caseating granulomas consistent with the granulomatous pattern of PACNS (Figure 2). Our patient was treated with oral prednisone and monthly intravenous cyclophosphamide (750mg/m2) for 12 months. There was improvement in his headache and balance. A neurological examination showed decreased tremor and dysmetria, and his gait had almost normalized. Follow-up brain and spine MRI scans showed improvement in the white matter hyperintensities on FLAIR imaging (Figure 1D) as well as on the gadolinium-enhanced images (Figure 1E,F).
